tb21_profile.skill: Obtain and extract a Debian source package, drive a C build (Makefile/configure) with an optional feature disabled (no X11), compile it, and install the binary to /usr/local/bin, then confirm it runs and lacks the excluded dependency
tb21_profile.domain: Linux from-source builds and Debian packaging: apt/dpkg source, make/autotools, feature flags, system install
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging: acquire source, configure a feature-toggled build, compile, install system-wide, verify

notes: This is a from-source build + feature-toggle + system-install task with a Debian-source-acquisition twist and a verify-the-binary step. TerminalWorld is the strongest pool: it is full of 'build C/C++ program X from source and install it system-wide' tasks, and tw_2077 (tree from tarball) and tw_17688 (VIM built with a specific feature set to a prefix) are the closest matches anywhere, the latter mirroring the no-X11 feature toggle. TMax contributes many 'fix a broken Makefile/configure then make install' vendored-package tasks, with task_000956 (fix configure, ./configure --prefix && make && make install) and task_000172 (make install into /usr/local/bin) especially on-point. Recursive-Task-Synthesis carries the Debian-packaging tooling (DEBIAN/control, dpkg --root) and configure-with-feature-flags builds. No corpus has the specific 'apt-get source / extract a Debian source package and build with X11 disabled' task, so the acquire-from-Debian aspect is covered only obliquely by the RTS deb-build tasks. SWE-Smith has no from-source build task; the conan AutotoolsToolchain / CMake-flag / GnuToolchain bugs are the nearest domain (getting a native build's compiler/linker flags right), judged on skill/domain as the spec directs. SWE-Rebench is weakest: setuptools/pipx/mkosi packaging bugs are the only build-adjacent items and they lose hard on task_form.
